title: Backup & restore
blurb: Back up files, restore from backup, move to a new computer, start fresh.

remedies.title: Time Machine backup failed or hasn't run
remedies.why: The backup drive is disconnected, full, or needs repair.

steps.text: Connect the backup drive and choose Back Up Now from the menu bar.
Check the drive in Disk Utility › First Aid.
If full, Time Machine deletes the oldest backups; a bigger drive helps.
Check Time Machine settings for the right disk.

remedies.title: Set up File History (versions of every file on an external drive)
remedies.why: File History keeps copies of your files every hour on an external drive.

steps.text: Plug in an external drive, open Control Panel › File History › Turn on.
Check Advanced settings for how often and how long to keep versions.
Restore with right-click › Restore previous versions.

remedies.title: Make a recovery USB drive
remedies.why: A recovery drive starts the computer when it won't boot.

steps.text: Search Start for "Create a recovery drive", or make install media with Microsoft's Media Creation Tool (16 GB USB).
Macs boot into Recovery without a USB; Apple's createinstallmedia makes a USB installer if needed.

remedies.title: Back up my photos safely
remedies.why: Photos are irreplaceable; keep at least two copies in different places.

steps.text: Turn on a cloud photo service (iCloud Photos, Google Photos, OneDrive camera upload).
Also copy them to an external drive once in a while.
Check the cloud copy opens before deleting anything from the phone.
